question.problem:
By changing the order of integration in the following repeated integrals so that they are integrated first with respect to $x,$ then $z,$ and then $y,$ express the following sum as a single repeated integral.

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2z}{\int }_{-y}^{z}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z+{\int }_{1}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{3-z}{\int }_{-y}^{z}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z
$$
question.worked_solution:
We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(y,z)}^{{u}_{2}(y,z)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y.
$$

From the repeated integrals, we see that the domain of integration $R={R}_{1}\cup {R}_{2},$ where ${R}_{1}$ and ${R}_{2}$ are type II regions, is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{1} & =\{(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le z\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le 2z,\,\,-y\le x\le z\}, \\ {R}_{2} & =\{(x,y,z)\,:\,1\le z\le 3,\,\,0\le y\le 3-z,\,\,-y\le x\le z\}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $x,$ the $x$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{-y}^{z}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y
$$

 

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $yz$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14234808/assets/9b8806738b61c4ce692f555261abcd9918096a7585291954a7f11c39aadeab39.png)

The region $D$ consists of two type II regions in the $yz$-plane:

$$
D=\{(y,z)\,:\,0\le z\le 1,\,0\le y\le 2z\}\,\cup \,\{(y,z)\,:\,1\le z\le 3,\,0\le y\le 3-z\}.
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z$ to $\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y,$ we write $D$ as a type I region.

Notice that the bottom boundary of the region, written in the form $z=z(y),$ is

$$
y=2z\,⟹\,z=\frac{y}{2}
$$

and the top boundary of the region is

$$
y=3-z\,⟹\,z=3-y.
$$

Then, the type I representation of the region is

$$
D=\{(y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 2,\,\frac{y}{2}\le z\le 3-y\},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14234808/assets/d1a9d83672ffbd372b6a994c62771291d957e6a5c13189a6baea6d544f6a1bbc.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{y/2}^{3-y}{\int }_{-y}^{z}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y.
$$
